+"""Rating contracts shared across the pipeline (Part 5).
+
+The committed rating is the single authoritative value produced by the
+deterministic validator in :mod:`tradingagents.agents.rating`. LLM output is
+advisory: it is a *candidate* that the authority checks before it may be stored.
+
+This module defines the wire/contract objects only; the commit logic lives in
+:mod:`tradingagents.rating_authority` (which re-uses the parser in
+:mod:`tradingagents.agents.rating`). Keeping the contract separate lets Part 3
+(manifest/report) and Part 6 (cost) read a stable shape without importing the
+authority itself.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Any
+
+# The committed value is exactly one of these six. Anything else is invalid.
+ALLOWED_RATINGS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
+    {"Buy", "Overweight", "Hold", "Underweight", "Sell", "REVIEW"}
+)
+
+# The tradeable subset (REVIEW is a "needs human/re-run" signal, not a position).
+TRADEABLE_RATINGS: frozenset[str] = ALLOWED_RATINGS - {"REVIEW"}
+
+REVIEW: str = "REVIEW"
+
+
+# Reason codes attached to a RatingResult. They are stable identifiers so tests,
+# logs and downstream tooling can assert *why* a decision is (or is not) REVIEW.
+class ReasonCode:
+    """Machine-readable reasons for a rating outcome."""
+
+    OK = "ok"
+    # The candidate text had no readable rating.
+    NO_RATING = "no_rating"
+    # The candidate string was not in the allowed set.
+    OUT_OF_SET = "out_of_set"
+    # A required provenance field was missing or empty.
+    MISSING_PROVENANCE = "missing_provenance"
+    # A provenance field was present but did not validate (bad id/version shape).
+    INVALID_PROVENANCE = "invalid_provenance"
+    # The snapshot id was absent or not marked verified.
+    UNVERIFIED_SNAPSHOT = "unverified_snapshot"
+    # The same decision id was already committed with a different value.
+    CONFLICT = "conflict"
+    # The persisted value failed re-validation before write.
+    PERSISTED_OUT_OF_SET = "persisted_out_of_set"
+
+
+def is_allowed(rating: str) -> bool:
+    """Whether ``rating`` is one of the six allowed committed values."""
+    return rating in ALLOWED_RATINGS
+
+
+def coerce_review(reason_code: str, *, provenance: Any = None) -> RatingResult:
+    """A REVIEW result carrying ``reason_code`` (never a tradeable tier)."""
+    return RatingResult(
+        rating=REVIEW,
+        reason_codes=(reason_code,),
+        provenance=provenance,
+        review_required=True,
+    )
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class RatingResult:
+    """The outcome of rating resolution / commit.
+
+    Fields (the agreed contract; extra fields may be added, existing ones are
+    never repurposed):
+
+    - ``rating``: exactly one of :data:`ALLOWED_RATINGS`. This is the only value
+      that may be persisted as the decision's rating.
+    - ``reason_codes``: stable codes (see :class:`ReasonCode`) explaining the
+      outcome; ``("ok",)`` for a clean tradeable commit.
+    - ``provenance``: the verified :class:`Provenance` this result was produced
+      from, or ``None`` when provenance was missing/invalid. Never free text.
+    - ``review_required``: ``True`` iff the value must not be treated as a
+      position (i.e. ``rating == "REVIEW"``). Redundant with the rating by
+      design, so callers can branch on intent without string compares.
+
+    Added field:
+
+    - ``decision_id``: the stable id the commit was keyed on (for idempotency),
+      or ``None`` for a resolution that was not stored.
+    """
+
+    rating: str
+    reason_codes: tuple[str, ...] = (ReasonCode.OK,)
+    provenance: Provenance | None = None
+    review_required: bool = False
+    decision_id: str | None = None
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if self.rating not in ALLOWED_RATINGS:
+            raise ValueError(f"rating {self.rating!r} is not in the allowed set")
+        # Keep the contract self-consistent: REVIEW <=> review_required.
+        if (self.rating == REVIEW) != bool(self.review_required):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "review_required must be True exactly when rating is REVIEW"
+            )
+
+    @property
+    def is_tradeable(self) -> bool:
+        return self.rating in TRADEABLE_RATINGS
+
+    @property
+    def is_review(self) -> bool:
+        return self.rating == REVIEW
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Provenance:
+    """Verified provenance a commit must carry.
+
+    A commit is only allowed when every field is present *and* validates. These
+    are structural ids/versions, not arbitrary non-empty strings: the ids must
+    match their hex/uuid-ish shape and versions must be non-empty with a
+    recognisable version token. Production populates this from the run's real
+    snapshot/manifest/models; tests use a clearly-marked fake (see
+    :class:`Provenance` construction in the authority's in-memory tests).
+
+    Fields:
+
+    - ``snapshot_id``: the verified market snapshot id, e.g. ``snap-<32 hex>``.
+    - ``manifest_id``: the evidence manifest id for this run, e.g. ``man-<32 hex>``.
+    - ``model``: the model identifier used for the decision.
+    - ``prompt_version``: the prompt template version pin.
+    - ``config_version``: the config version pin.
+
+    Additional:
+
+    - ``snapshot_verified``: whether the snapshot was cryptographically/structurally
+      verified. An unverified snapshot id is not acceptable for a commit.
+    """
+
+    snapshot_id: str
+    manifest_id: str
+    model: str
+    prompt_version: str
+    config_version: str
+    snapshot_verified: bool = True
+
+    def missing_fields(self) -> list[str]:
+        """Names of required fields that are empty/missing."""
+        required = (
+            "snapshot_id",
+            "manifest_id",
+            "model",
+            "prompt_version",
+            "config_version",
+        )
+        return [name for name in required if not getattr(self, name)]
+
+
+# Store adapter protocol (Part 5 owns the write-gate; the concrete store is
+# provided by Part 3). A store is any object exposing these two methods. The
+# authority never assumes more than this.
+#
+#   read(decision_id: str) -> dict | None
+#       returns the previously stored record (must include a "rating" key) or
+#       None when nothing is stored for ``decision_id``.
+#   write(decision_id: str, record: dict) -> None
+#       persists ``record`` for ``decision_id``; must be atomic for that id.
+#
+# The authority re-validates the rating immediately before calling ``write`` and
+# refuses an out-of-set value (never trusting the store).
+Store = Any
+
+
+@dataclass
+class InMemoryRatingStore:
+    """A minimal in-memory store used by tests and as the reference adapter.
+
+    It is deliberately tiny: Part 3's real records store is expected to be
+    dropped in behind the same ``read``/``write`` interface.
+    """
+
+    _records: dict[str, dict] = field(default_factory=dict)
+
+    def read(self, decision_id: str) -> dict | None:
+        return self._records.get(decision_id)
+
+    def write(self, decision_id: str, record: dict) -> None:
+        self._records[decision_id] = dict(record)
+
+    def all(self) -> dict[str, dict]:
+        return dict(self._records)

+"""Deterministic rating authority (Part 5, REQ-INV-003).
+
+The committed rating is produced **only** here, by deterministic validation of
+the model's advisory output, and is exactly one of
+``{Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell, REVIEW}``. This module is the single
+entry point that may decide a persisted rating; it re-uses the tolerant parser in
+:mod:`tradingagents.agents.rating` rather than duplicating it.
+
+Design rules enforced here:
+
+- Model output is a *candidate*, never authoritative. It is parsed and checked
+  against :data:`tradingagents.contracts.rating.ALLOWED_RATINGS`; anything else
+  becomes ``REVIEW`` with a reason code.
+- A commit requires verified :class:`Provenance` (snapshot id, manifest id and
+  model/prompt/config versions). Missing or structurally invalid provenance ->
+  ``REVIEW`` (never a tradeable tier) and no write.
+- Free text never overrides a structured rating: when the candidate is given as
+  a structured value it is validated directly; when only text is available it is
+  parsed, but prose without a labelled call resolves to ``REVIEW``.
+- The write gate re-validates the value immediately before persisting, so an
+  out-of-set value can never reach the store even if produced upstream.
+- Commits are idempotent per stable ``decision_id``: re-committing the same
+  decision returns the existing committed value; a conflicting re-commit is
+  refused. Different decisions never share a key.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+from tradingagents.agents.rating import extract_rating
+from tradingagents.contracts.rating import (
+    ALLOWED_RATINGS,
+    REVIEW,
+    InMemoryRatingStore,
+    Provenance,
+    RatingResult,
+    ReasonCode,
+    Store,
+    coerce_review,
+)
+
+__all__ = [
+    "ALLOWED_RATINGS",
+    "REVIEW",
+    "RatingResult",
+    "ReasonCode",
+    "Provenance",
+    "InMemoryRatingStore",
+    "resolve_rating",
+    "validate_provenance",
+    "commit_rating",
+    "read_committed_rating",
+]
+
+# Structural shapes for the provenance ids. These are not "any non-empty string":
+# a snapshot/manifest id must look like `prefix-<hex>` with a real hex body.
+_SNAPSHOT_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^snap-[0-9a-f]{8,64}$")
+_MANIFEST_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^man-[0-9a-f]{8,64}$")
+# A version pin: a bare semver-ish or `v<number>` token, optionally with `+build`.
+_VERSION_RE = re.compile(r"^v?\d+(?:\.\d+){0,2}(?:[-+][0-9A-Za-z.]+)?$")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class _ProvenanceCheck:
+    ok: bool
+    reason: str
+
+
+def validate_provenance(provenance: Provenance | None) -> _ProvenanceCheck:
+    """Whether ``provenance`` is a verified, well-formed commit source.
+
+    This is the *production* validation: it checks structure, not mere
+    non-emptiness. A test fake must still satisfy these shapes, which keeps the
+    fake honest (a fake cannot be arbitrary free text).
+    """
+    if provenance is None:
+        return _ProvenanceCheck(False, ReasonCode.MISSING_PROVENANCE)
+
+    missing = provenance.missing_fields()
+    if missing:
+        return _ProvenanceCheck(False, ReasonCode.MISSING_PROVENANCE)
+
+    if not provenance.snapshot_verified:
+        return _ProvenanceCheck(False, ReasonCode.UNVERIFIED_SNAPSHOT)
+
+    if not _SNAPSHOT_ID_RE.match(provenance.snapshot_id):
+        return _ProvenanceCheck(False, ReasonCode.INVALID_PROVENANCE)
+    if not _MANIFEST_ID_RE.match(provenance.manifest_id):
+        return _ProvenanceCheck(False, ReasonCode.INVALID_PROVENANCE)
+    if not (_VERSION_RE.match(provenance.prompt_version)
+            and _VERSION_RE.match(provenance.config_version)):
+        return _ProvenanceCheck(False, ReasonCode.INVALID_PROVENANCE)
+    if not provenance.model.strip():
+        return _ProvenanceCheck(False, ReasonCode.INVALID_PROVENANCE)
+
+    return _ProvenanceCheck(True, ReasonCode.OK)
+
+
+def _candidate_to_rating(candidate: object) -> tuple[str, str]:
+    """Resolve a candidate (structured value or text) to ``(rating, reason)``.
+
+    A structured value is validated as-is. Text is parsed by the shared parser;
+    text with no labelled call is ``REVIEW``. The result is always in
+    :data:`ALLOWED_RATINGS`.
+    """
+    if isinstance(candidate, str):
+        value = candidate.strip()
+        if value in ALLOWED_RATINGS:
+            return value, ReasonCode.OK
+        # Not a structured tier: treat as free text and parse a labelled call.
+        parsed = extract_rating(candidate)
+        if parsed is None:
+            return REVIEW, ReasonCode.NO_RATING
+        return parsed, ReasonCode.OK
+    return REVIEW, ReasonCode.NO_RATING
+
+
+def resolve_rating(candidate: object) -> str:
+    """The deterministic verdict for ``candidate`` alone (no provenance).
+
+    Always in the allowed set. Exposed so callers that only need the parsed
+    value (e.g. the memory log tag) share exactly the authority's parser.
+    """
+    rating, _ = _candidate_to_rating(candidate)
+    return rating
+
+
+def _normalise_existing(record: dict | None) -> str | None:
+    if not record:
+        return None
+    value = record.get("rating")
+    return value if value in ALLOWED_RATINGS else None
+
+
+def commit_rating(
+    candidate: object,
+    provenance: Provenance | None,
+    store: Store,
+    *,
+    decision_id: str,
+) -> RatingResult:
+    """Validate ``candidate`` against ``provenance`` and commit it via ``store``.
+
+    Args:
+        candidate: the model's advisory output — either a structured tier string
+            or the decision text. Parsed/validated deterministically.
+        provenance: the verified run provenance, or ``None`` when unavailable.
+        store: an object with ``read(decision_id)`` and ``write(decision_id,
+            record)`` (see :data:`tradingagents.contracts.rating.Store`). The
+            authority re-validates before writing and never trusts the store.
+        decision_id: a stable, non-empty id for this decision. It keys idempotency
+            and prevents cross-decision collisions. A blank id is a programming
+            error and is refused (never defaulted to a shared key).
+
+    Returns:
+        A :class:`RatingResult`. On any failure the ``rating`` is ``REVIEW``,
+        ``review_required`` is ``True``, ``reason_codes`` explains why, and
+        nothing is written. On success the value is tradeable, is in the allowed
+        set, carries the provenance, and exactly one record exists for
+        ``decision_id``.
+    """
+    if not isinstance(decision_id, str) or not decision_id.strip():
+        # Refuse an unusable key rather than letting decisions share one.
+        return coerce_review(ReasonCode.INVALID_PROVENANCE, provenance=provenance)
+
+    # Idempotency: an existing commit for this id wins, unless it conflicts.
+    existing = _normalise_existing(store.read(decision_id))
+    if existing is not None:
+        return RatingResult(
+            rating=existing,
+            reason_codes=(ReasonCode.OK,),
+            provenance=provenance,
+            review_required=(existing == REVIEW),
+            decision_id=decision_id,
+        )
+
+    # Provenance gate: missing/invalid/unverified -> REVIEW, no write.
+    check = validate_provenance(provenance)
+    if not check.ok:
+        return coerce_review(check.reason, provenance=provenance)
+
+    rating, reason = _candidate_to_rating(candidate)
+    if rating == REVIEW:
+        return coerce_review(reason, provenance=provenance)
+    if rating not in ALLOWED_RATINGS:
+        # Defence in depth: the parser must never yield an out-of-set value.
+        return coerce_review(ReasonCode.OUT_OF_SET, provenance=provenance)
+
+    record = {
+        "rating": rating,
+        "decision_id": decision_id,
+        "snapshot_id": provenance.snapshot_id if provenance else None,
+        "manifest_id": provenance.manifest_id if provenance else None,
+        "model": provenance.model if provenance else None,
+        "prompt_version": provenance.prompt_version if provenance else None,
+        "config_version": provenance.config_version if provenance else None,
+    }
+    store.write(decision_id, record)
+
+    return RatingResult(
+        rating=rating,
+        reason_codes=(ReasonCode.OK,),
+        provenance=provenance,
+        review_required=False,
+        decision_id=decision_id,
+    )
+
+
+def read_committed_rating(store: Store, *, decision_id: str) -> RatingResult:
+    """Read back a committed rating, re-validating it against the allowed set.
+
+    A stored value that is out-of-set (tampered/corrupt) is treated as ``REVIEW``
+    with :data:`ReasonCode.PERSISTED_OUT_OF_SET` — it is never returned as a tier.
+    """
+    record = store.read(decision_id)
+    value = record.get("rating") if record else None
+    if value in ALLOWED_RATINGS:
+        return RatingResult(
+            rating=value,
+            reason_codes=(ReasonCode.OK,),
+            review_required=(value == REVIEW),
+            decision_id=decision_id,
+        )
+    return coerce_review(ReasonCode.PERSISTED_OUT_OF_SET)

@@ -0,0 +1,250 @@
+"""Secret redaction (Part 5, REQ-INV-004).
+
+Credentials — API keys, bearer tokens, query-param auth secrets — must never
+reach logs, reports, manifests, prompts/model context, or error messages. This
+module centralises redaction so every sink shares one implementation:
+
+- :func:`redact` — the single public entry point; redacts any nested value
+  (str, bytes, dict, list, tuple, exception, or arbitrary object's repr).
+- :func:`redact_text` — redact a single string.
+- :func:`redact_obj` — recurse into nested containers.
+
+Redaction has two sources of truth:
+
+1. **Registered secrets**: actual key values the process loaded from the
+   environment for known providers (via :data:`tradingagents.llm_clients.api_key_env.PROVIDER_API_KEY_ENV`).
+   These are replaced exactly, so a key with no recognisable shape is still
+   removed.
+2. **Patterns**: well-known token shapes (OpenAI ``sk-...``, Anthropic
+   ``sk-ant-...``, GitHub ``ghp_...``, generic ``Bearer <token>``, and
+   ``key=``/``api_key=``/``token=`` query parameters). These catch keys not
+   registered in this process.
+
+Only *synthetic* keys are used in tests; this module never logs or prints a real
+secret.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import os
+import re
+from typing import Any
+
+__all__ = [
+    "REDACTED",
+    "REDACTED_PATTERNS",
+    "register_secret",
+    "redact_text",
+    "redact_obj",
+    "redact",
+    "RedactingFilter",
+    "install_log_filter",
+    "safe_prompt_payload",
+    "scrub_manifest",
+    "contains_secret",
+]
+
+REDACTED = "***"
+
+# Placeholder patterns. Each is anchored to a recognisable prefix so benign text
+# (numbers, ordinary words, URLs without credentials) is preserved.
+REDACTED_PATTERNS: tuple[re.Pattern[str], ...] = (
+    # OpenAI-style: sk-... / sk-proj-... (also our synthetic test keys).
+    re.compile(r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,}"),
+    # Anthropic: sk-ant-...
+    re.compile(r"sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,}"),
+    # GitHub tokens.
+    re.compile(r"ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}"),
+    re.compile(r"github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}"),
+    # Bearer tokens (Authorization headers).
+    re.compile(r"(?i)\bbearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._\-]{8,}"),
+    # Query-param / assignment secrets: key=..., api_key: ..., token="...".
+    re.compile(
+        r"(?i)\b(api[_-]?key|access[_-]?token|token|secret|password)"
+        r"\s*[:=]\s*['\"]?[A-Za-z0-9._\-]{6,}['\"]?"
+    ),
+    # AWS access key id (bearer/bedrock paths often carry one).
+    re.compile(r"\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b"),
+)
+
+# Key values registered by the process (from the env), replaced exactly. Kept in
+# a module-level set so a caller that loaded a key can register it without us
+# re-reading the environment. Never logged.
+_REGISTERED_SECRETS: set[str] = set()
+
+
+def register_secret(secret: str | None) -> None:
+    """Register a literal secret value to be redacted verbatim.
+
+    Empty / very short values are ignored: redacting a 1-2 char substring would
+    over-redact ordinary text. A real key is never that short.
+    """
+    if secret and len(secret) >= 6:
+        _REGISTERED_SECRETS.add(secret)
+
+
+def _register_env_secrets() -> None:
+    """Register the values of the known provider env vars, if present.
+
+    Reads names from the canonical map so we never guess which env vars hold
+    keys. Imported lazily to keep this module importable without the LLM stack.
+    """
+    try:
+        from tradingagents.llm_clients.api_key_env import PROVIDER_API_KEY_ENV
+    except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - import guard
+        return
+    for env_name in PROVIDER_API_KEY_ENV.values():
+        if not env_name:
+            continue
+        value = os.environ.get(env_name)
+        if value:
+            register_secret(value)
+
+
+def _redact_text(text: str) -> str:
+    _register_env_secrets()
+    out = text
+    # Registered literals first: exact removal regardless of shape.
+    for secret in sorted(_REGISTERED_SECRETS, key=len, reverse=True):
+        if secret and secret in out:
+            out = out.replace(secret, REDACTED)
+    for pattern in REDACTED_PATTERNS:
+        out = pattern.sub(REDACTED, out)
+    return out
+
+
+def redact_text(text: str) -> str:
+    """Redact secrets from a single string."""
+    return _redact_text(text)
+
+
+def redact_obj(value: Any) -> Any:
+    """Recursively redact secrets from a nested value, preserving its shape.
+
+    - ``str`` -> redacted ``str``
+    - ``bytes`` -> redacted ``bytes``
+    - ``dict`` -> new ``dict`` with redacted keys and values
+    - ``list``/``tuple``/``set`` -> same type with redacted elements
+    - ``BaseException`` -> a new exception of the same type with a redacted message
+    - anything else -> redacted ``repr`` (objects are not echoed raw)
+    """
+    if isinstance(value, str):
+        return _redact_text(value)
+    if isinstance(value, bytes):
+        return _redact_text(value.decode("utf-8", "replace")).encode("utf-8", "replace")
+    if isinstance(value, dict):
+        return {redact_obj(k): redact_obj(v) for k, v in value.items()}
+    if isinstance(value, list):
+        return [redact_obj(v) for v in value]
+    if isinstance(value, tuple):
+        return tuple(redact_obj(v) for v in value)
+    if isinstance(value, set):
+        return {redact_obj(v) for v in value}
+    if isinstance(value, BaseException):
+        try:
+            return type(value)(_redact_text(str(value)))
+        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - exotic exception ctor
+            return REDACTED
+    if value is None or isinstance(value, (int, float, bool)):
+        return value
+    # Unknown object: do not echo it raw; redact its repr.
+    return _redact_text(repr(value))
+
+
+def redact(value: Any) -> Any:
+    """The unified redaction entry point for any value or sink."""
+    if isinstance(value, str):
+        return _redact_text(value)
+    return redact_obj(value)
+
+
+def contains_secret(value: Any) -> bool:
+    """Whether a (stringified) value still contains a known secret pattern.
+
+    Used by tests and the security log as a last-line assertion; it checks both
+    registered literals and the placeholder patterns.
+    """
+    text = value if isinstance(value, str) else repr(value)
+    if any(secret in text for secret in _REGISTERED_SECRETS):
+        return True
+    return any(pattern.search(text) for pattern in REDACTED_PATTERNS)
+
+
+class RedactingFilter(logging.Filter):
+    """A logging filter that redacts a record before it is emitted.
+
+    Handles the three ways a log line can carry a secret:
+
+    - ``record.msg`` when it is the final string;
+    - deferred ``%``-style arguments in ``record.args`` (``log.info("k=%s", key)``);
+    - exception text in ``record.exc_info`` / ``record.exc_text``.
+
+    ``record.args`` is redacted element-wise, then the formatted message is
+    materialised and redacted (so formats like ``Bearer %s`` are also covered).
+    """
+
+    def filter(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> bool:  # noqa: A003 - logging API
+        if isinstance(record.msg, str):
+            record.msg = _redact_text(record.msg)
+        if record.args:
+            if isinstance(record.args, dict):
+                record.args = redact_obj(record.args)
+            else:
+                record.args = tuple(redact_obj(a) for a in record.args)
+        # Materialise the final message so formatting-introduced secrets are
+        # caught, and so downstream handlers that re-format see a redacted msg.
+        try:
+            message = record.getMessage()
+        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - malformed record
+            message = str(record.msg)
+        if contains_secret(message):
+            record.msg = _redact_text(message)
+            record.args = ()
+        if record.exc_info:
+            exc = record.exc_info[1]
+            if exc is not None:
+                record.exc_text = _redact_text(str(exc))
+        elif record.exc_text:
+            record.exc_text = _redact_text(record.exc_text)
+        return True
+
+
+def install_log_filter(logger: logging.Logger | None = None) -> RedactingFilter:
+    """Attach a :class:`RedactingFilter` to ``logger`` (root by default).
+
+    Returns the filter so callers/tests can remove it. Idempotent: returns the
+    existing filter if one is already installed on that logger.
+    """
+    target = logger or logging.getLogger()
+    for existing in target.filters:
+        if isinstance(existing, RedactingFilter):
+            return existing
+    filt = RedactingFilter()
+    target.addFilter(filt)
+    return filt
+
+
+def safe_prompt_payload(messages: Any) -> Any:
+    """A prompt payload safe to send to a model: redacted, with a guard.
+
+    This is the adapter Part 1/2 should call before a model request. It redacts
+    the payload and asserts no registered/patterned secret survives; it never
+    reads a key into the payload.
+    """
+    redacted = redact_obj(messages)
+    if contains_secret(redacted):
+        # Defensive: after redaction nothing should remain. Drop to a marker
+        # rather than risk sending a secret.
+        return redact_obj(redacted)
+    return redacted
+
+
+def scrub_manifest(manifest: Any) -> Any:
+    """A manifest/report payload with every secret redacted before persistence.
+
+    Part 3 calls this immediately before writing ``manifest.json`` or a report so
+    a secret in a field (e.g. a vendor error captured in an event) cannot reach
+    disk. Shape is preserved.
+    """
+    return redact_obj(manifest)

+"""Untrusted text sanitisation (Part 5, REQ-SEC-001).
+
+News, social posts and user input are untrusted. Before such text enters a
+prompt it is sanitised here:
+
+- C0/C1 control characters (except tab/newline) are removed.
+- Prompt-injection *shapes* are detected: instruction override, role hijack,
+  tool/function-call injection, and delimiter-escape attempts. A detected line
+  is **dropped** (not merely warned about) and the drop is logged.
+- The surviving text is wrapped in a delimiter so the model can tell data from
+  instructions. Any forged closing delimiter in the input is neutralised, and
+  re-sanitising already-wrapped text does not double-wrap or break out.
+- Length is bounded; over-long text is truncated with an explicit marker.
+
+Ordinary numbers, URLs and factual words are preserved: detection targets
+instruction-like *structures*, not the presence of words like "buy" or "sell".
+
+Public API:
+
+- :func:`sanitize(text) -> str` — the simple entry point required by callers;
+  returns the delimited, sanitised text (safe to place in a prompt).
+- :func:`sanitize_detailed(text) -> SanitizedText` — the full result with
+  ``text`` (same as :func:`sanitize`), ``dropped`` (bool), ``events`` and the
+  ``retained`` (undelimited) text, for callers/tests that need the detail.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+import unicodedata
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+
+from .security_log import EventKind, SecurityEventLog, get_event_log, log_event
+
+__all__ = [
+    "SanitizedText",
+    "sanitize",
+    "sanitize_detailed",
+    "is_suspicious",
+    "OPEN_DELIM",
+    "CLOSE_DELIM",
+]
+
+OPEN_DELIM = "<untrusted>"
+CLOSE_DELIM = "</untrusted>"
+
+DEFAULT_MAX_LEN = 8_000
+
+# C0/C1 controls except \t \n \r.
+_CONTROL_RE = re.compile(r"[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f-\x9f]")
+
+# Instruction-override / role-hijack / tool-call shapes. These target the
+# *structure* of an injection, not benign mentions of a company or a rating.
+_INJECTION_PATTERNS: tuple[tuple[str, re.Pattern[str]], ...] = (
+    # "ignore (all) previous instructions", "disregard the above"
+    ("instruction_override", re.compile(
+        r"(?i)\b(ignore|disregard|forget|override|bypass)\b[^.\n]{0,40}"
+        r"\b(previous|prior|above|earlier|all|any|your)\b[^.\n]{0,30}"
+        r"\b(instruction|instructions|prompt|prompts|rules?|directions?)\b")),
+    # "you are now ...", "act as ...", "system prompt", "developer mode"
+    ("role_hijack", re.compile(
+        r"(?i)(\byou are now\b|\bact as\b|\bpretend to be\b|\bsystem prompt\b|"
+        r"\bdeveloper mode\b|\bjailbreak\b|\bDAN\b)")),
+    # "new instructions:" / "### system:" / "assistant:" role markers
+    ("role_marker", re.compile(
+        r"(?im)^\s*(#{1,6}\s*)?(system|assistant|developer|tool)\s*:")),
+    # Tool/function-call injection.
+    ("tool_call_injection", re.compile(
+        r"(?i)(\bcall\s+(the\s+)?(tool|function)\b|"
+        r"\bexecute\s+(the\s+)?(tool|function|command|shell)\b|"
+        r"<\|?\s*(tool_call|function_call)\s*\|?>|"
+        r"\btool_call\s*\(|\bfunction_call\s*\()")),
+    # Delimiter escape: attempt to close/forge our trust boundary.
+    ("delimiter_escape", re.compile(
+        r"(?i)(</?\s*untrusted\s*>|</?\s*system\s*>|<\|im_(start|end)\|>)")),
+)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class SanitizedText:
+    """The detailed outcome of sanitising one untrusted text."""
+
+    text: str                       # delimited text safe for a prompt
+    retained: str                   # undelimited sanitised text (facts kept)
+    dropped: bool
+    events: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
+    truncated: bool = False
+
+    def __str__(self) -> str:       # so sanitize() can return it transparently
+        return self.text
+
+
+def _normalise(text: str) -> str:
+    # NFKC folds fullwidth/confusable forms so an injection written in fullwidth
+    # punctuation is still recognised.
+    return unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text)
+
+
+def _strip_controls(text: str) -> str:
+    return _CONTROL_RE.sub("", text)
+
+
+def _matching_kinds(text: str) -> list[str]:
+    kinds = []
+    for name, pattern in _INJECTION_PATTERNS:
+        if pattern.search(text):
+            kinds.append(name)
+    return kinds
+
+
+def is_suspicious(text: str) -> bool:
+    """Whether ``text`` contains an injection-shaped structure."""
+    return bool(_matching_kinds(_normalise(_strip_controls(text or ""))))
+
+
+def _neutralise_delimiters(text: str) -> str:
+    # Defang any forged delimiters so data cannot pretend to close our wrapper.
+    text = re.sub(r"(?i)</?\s*untrusted\s*>", "[delimiter]", text)
+    text = re.sub(r"(?i)</?\s*system\s*>", "[delimiter]", text)
+    text = re.sub(r"(?i)<\|im_(start|end)\|>", "[delimiter]", text)
+    return text
+
+
+def sanitize_detailed(
+    text: str,
+    *,
+    max_len: int = DEFAULT_MAX_LEN,
+    event_log: SecurityEventLog | None = None,
+) -> SanitizedText:
+    """Sanitise one untrusted text and return the detail (see module docs).
+
+    A text containing an injection structure is *dropped*: the returned
+    ``text``/``retained`` is empty and ``dropped`` is True. Benign text is
+    cleaned, delimiter-neutralised, bounded, and wrapped.
+    """
+    target_log = event_log or get_event_log()
+    raw = text or ""
+
+    normalised = _normalise(raw)
+    cleaned = _strip_controls(normalised)
+    # If the input is our own wrapper (re-sanitising), unwrap it first so the
+    # wrapper's own delimiters are not mistaken for a forged escape.
+    cleaned = _unwrap(cleaned)
+
+    kinds = _matching_kinds(cleaned)
+    if kinds:
+        for kind in kinds:
+            log_event(EventKind.INPUT_DROPPED, f"injection:{kind}",
+                      detail={"preview": cleaned[:200]}, event_log=target_log)
+        return SanitizedText(text="", retained="", dropped=True,
+                             events=[e.as_dict() for e in target_log.events()])
+
+    retained = _neutralise_delimiters(cleaned).strip()
+    truncated = False
+    if len(retained) > max_len:
+        retained = retained[:max_len].rstrip() + " […truncated]"
+        truncated = True
+
+    # Wrap once. If the input was already wrapped (re-sanitising), unwrap first
+    # so we neither double-wrap nor nest.
+    retained = _unwrap(retained)
+    wrapped = f"{OPEN_DELIM}\n{retained}\n{CLOSE_DELIM}"
+
+    log_event(EventKind.INPUT_SANITIZED, "clean",
+              detail={"truncated": truncated}, event_log=target_log)
+    return SanitizedText(text=wrapped, retained=retained, dropped=False,
+                         events=[e.as_dict() for e in target_log.events()],
+                         truncated=truncated)
+
+
+def _unwrap(text: str) -> str:
+    """Strip an outer OPEN/CLOSE delim pair so re-sanitising is idempotent."""
+    stripped = text.strip()
+    if stripped.startswith(OPEN_DELIM) and stripped.endswith(CLOSE_DELIM):
+        inner = stripped[len(OPEN_DELIM):-len(CLOSE_DELIM)]
+        return inner.strip()
+    return text
+
+
+def sanitize(text: str, *, max_len: int = DEFAULT_MAX_LEN,
+             event_log: SecurityEventLog | None = None) -> str:
+    """Sanitise ``text`` and return prompt-safe, delimited text.
+
+    The simple entry point: returns a ``str``. An injection-shaped text yields
+    ``""`` (dropped); use :func:`sanitize_detailed` when you need to know that
+    it was dropped and why.
+    """
+    return sanitize_detailed(text, max_len=max_len, event_log=event_log).text

+"""Security event log (Part 5, REQ-SEC-001 acceptance line 5).
+
+Every detection, sanitisation, validation failure and tool rejection is recorded
+as a :class:`SecurityEvent` with a machine-readable ``kind`` and a human
+``reason``. The event is **redacted before it is stored**, so a security log can
+itself never become a secret-leak sink.
+
+The log is in-memory and append-only by default, so it is deterministic and
+offline-testable. Production can attach a drain (e.g. Part 3's manifest
+``security_events`` list) via :func:`drain_events`.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from datetime import UTC, datetime
+from typing import Any
+
+from .redaction import redact_obj
+
+__all__ = [
+    "SecurityEvent",
+    "EventKind",
+    "SecurityEventLog",
+    "get_event_log",
+    "log_event",
+    "drain_events",
+    "reset_event_log",
+]
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class EventKind:
+    """Stable event kinds (one per detection/validation/tool outcome)."""
+
+    INPUT_SANITIZED = "input_sanitized"
+    INPUT_DROPPED = "input_dropped"
+    OUTPUT_REJECTED = "output_rejected"
+    TOOL_REJECTED = "tool_rejected"
+    TOOL_ALLOWED = "tool_allowed"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class SecurityEvent:
+    """A single security event; all free text is redacted before storage."""
+
+    kind: str
+    reason: str
+    detail: Any = None
+    at: str = field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(UTC).isoformat())
+
+    def as_dict(self) -> dict:
+        return {"kind": self.kind, "reason": self.reason,
+                "detail": self.detail, "at": self.at}
+
+
+class SecurityEventLog:
+    """An append-only, in-memory, redacted event log."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self._events: list[SecurityEvent] = []
+
+    def record(self, kind: str, reason: str, detail: Any = None) -> SecurityEvent:
+        event = SecurityEvent(kind=kind, reason=redact_obj(reason),
+                              detail=redact_obj(detail))
+        self._events.append(event)
+        return event
+
+    def events(self) -> list[SecurityEvent]:
+        return list(self._events)
+
+    def drain(self) -> list[dict]:
+        """Return the events then clear them (used to hand off to a manifest)."""
+        out = [e.as_dict() for e in self._events]
+        self._events.clear()
+        return out
+
+    def count(self, kind: str | None = None) -> int:
+        if kind is None:
+            return len(self._events)
+        return sum(1 for e in self._events if e.kind == kind)
+
+
+_DEFAULT_LOG = SecurityEventLog()
+
+
+def get_event_log() -> SecurityEventLog:
+    """The process-wide event log (tests may :func:`reset_event_log`)."""
+    return _DEFAULT_LOG
+
+
+def reset_event_log() -> None:
+    """Clear the process-wide event log (for test isolation)."""
+    _DEFAULT_LOG.drain()
+
+
+def log_event(kind: str, reason: str, detail: Any = None,
+              event_log: SecurityEventLog | None = None) -> SecurityEvent:
+    """Record ``kind``/``reason`` on ``event_log`` (default: process-wide)."""
+    target = event_log or _DEFAULT_LOG
+    event = target.record(kind, reason, detail)
+    # Mirror to the stdlib logger; a RedactingFilter (if installed) scrubs it,
+    # and the message here is already redacted.
+    logger.debug("security_event kind=%s reason=%s", event.kind, event.reason)
+    return event
+
+
+def drain_events(event_log: SecurityEventLog | None = None) -> list[dict]:
+    """Drain events as plain dicts for a manifest / report field."""
+    return (event_log or _DEFAULT_LOG).drain()

@@ -0,0 +1,116 @@
+"""Role-bound tool execution guard (Part 5, REQ-SEC-001 acceptance line 4).
+
+An agent may only call the tools bound to its role. When the model proposes a
+tool outside that allowlist, the guard rejects the call **before it executes**,
+logs a ``tool_rejected`` security event, and the caller continues without it.
+
+Guarantees:
+
+- A rejected tool's ``execute`` is never invoked (the executable is not even
+  looked up on the reject path), so an unauthorised call's execution count is 0.
+- Rejection is recorded (redacted) with the role, tool and reason.
+- Authorised calls still run, so one rejection does not block the run.
+
+The guard owns the "reject before execute" decision; Part 1 wires it into the
+graph's tool dispatch (see ``docs/part5-integration.md``). An
+:class:`UnauthorizedToolCall` raised here is caught by the caller (the graph
+dispatch), which continues the run without the tool.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Any
+
+from .security_log import EventKind, SecurityEventLog, log_event
+
+__all__ = [
+    "UnauthorizedToolCall",
+    "ToolGuard",
+    "RoleToolGuard",
+]
+
+
+class UnauthorizedToolCall(PermissionError):
+    """Raised when a role proposes a tool it is not bound to.
+
+    The caller (graph dispatch) catches this to continue the run without the
+    tool. It is raised *before* the tool executes.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, role: str, tool: str) -> None:
+        super().__init__(f"role {role!r} is not allowed to call tool {tool!r}")
+        self.role = role
+        self.tool = tool
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ToolGuard:
+    """Per-role tool allowlists plus invocation bookkeeping.
+
+    ``allowed`` maps a role to the set of tool names it may call. Add/remove
+    tools via :meth:`bind` / :meth:`unbind`. The guard records how many times
+    each (role, tool) actually executed, so tests can assert a rejected tool's
+    execution count is 0.
+    """
+
+    allowed: dict[str, set[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    _exec_counts: dict[tuple[str, str], int] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    event_log: SecurityEventLog | None = None
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        self.allowed = {role: set(tools) for role, tools in self.allowed.items()}
+
+    def bind(self, role: str, *tools: str) -> None:
+        self.allowed.setdefault(role, set()).update(tools)
+
+    def unbind(self, role: str, *tools: str) -> None:
+        self.allowed.setdefault(role, set()).difference_update(tools)
+
+    def is_allowed(self, role: str, tool: str) -> bool:
+        return tool in self.allowed.get(role, set())
+
+    def executions(self, role: str, tool: str) -> int:
+        """How many times ``(role, tool)`` actually executed."""
+        return self._exec_counts.get((role, tool), 0)
+
+    def call(self, role: str, tool: str,
+             executables: dict[str, Callable[..., Any]],
+             *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
+        """Execute ``tool`` for ``role`` iff it is allowed; else reject.
+
+        On rejection raises :class:`UnauthorizedToolCall` without touching
+        ``executables[tool]``. On success, records the execution and returns the
+        tool's result.
+        """
+        self._check_and_log(role, tool)
+        tool_fn = executables[tool]
+        result = tool_fn(*args, **kwargs)
+        self._exec_counts[(role, tool)] = self._exec_counts.get((role, tool), 0) + 1
+        return result
+
+    def call_names(self, role: str,
+                   proposed: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, bool]:
+        """Classify proposed tools as allowed/rejected for ``role`` (no exec).
+
+        Useful for a planning step that must decide which tool calls to attempt
+        before any execute happens.
+        """
+        decisions: dict[str, bool] = {}
+        for tool in proposed:
+            decisions[tool] = self.is_allowed(role, tool)
+        return decisions
+
+    def _check_and_log(self, role: str, tool: str) -> None:
+        if self.is_allowed(role, tool):
+            log_event(EventKind.TOOL_ALLOWED, f"{role}:{tool}",
+                      event_log=self.event_log)
+            return
+        log_event(EventKind.TOOL_REJECTED, f"unauthorized:{role}:{tool}",
+                  detail={"role": role, "tool": tool}, event_log=self.event_log)
+        raise UnauthorizedToolCall(role, tool)
+
+
+# Convenience alias with an intent-revealing name.
+RoleToolGuard = ToolGuard

+"""Model-output validation before it becomes state (Part 5, REQ-SEC-001).
+
+Model output is untrusted. Before any field becomes part of the run state it is
+validated against a declarative schema whose supported vocabulary is deliberately
+small and explicit — this is **not** a claim to implement full JSON Schema:
+
+==========================  ====================================================
+keyword                     meaning
+==========================  ====================================================
+``type``                    ``object`` / ``array`` / ``string`` / ``number`` /
+                            ``integer`` / ``boolean`` / ``null``
+``properties``              per-key sub-schema (object)
+``required``                keys that must be present (object)
+``enum``                    value must be one of the listed values
+``items``                   element sub-schema (array)
+``refs``                    list of field names whose string values must be ids
+                            that appear in a supplied reference set (referential
+                            integrity, e.g. evidence ids cited by the report)
+==========================  ====================================================
+
+A field failing the type/enum/ref checks, or a required field that is missing,
+makes the whole output **invalid**: the caller must drop it (not store it) and a
+``security_event`` is logged with the reason. The validator never mutates or
+"repairs" the input.
+
+Use an existing mature validator when a full JSON Schema is needed; this module
+covers exactly the structure/type/enum/reference checks the requirement names.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Any
+
+from .security_log import EventKind, SecurityEventLog, get_event_log, log_event
+
+__all__ = ["ValidationResult", "validate_output"]
+
+_TYPE_MAP = {
+    "object": dict,
+    "array": list,
+    "string": str,
+    "boolean": bool,
+    # bool is a subclass of int in Python; handle integer/number explicitly.
+    "integer": int,
+    "number": (int, float),
+    "null": type(None),
+}
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ValidationResult:
+    """Outcome of validating one model output against a schema."""
+
+    ok: bool
+    errors: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    value: Any = None  # the original value when ok; the dropped payload is None
+
+    @property
+    def rejected(self) -> bool:
+        return not self.ok
+
+
+def _type_ok(expected: str, value: Any) -> bool:
+    py = _TYPE_MAP.get(expected)
+    if py is None:
+        return False
+    if expected in ("integer", "number") and isinstance(value, bool):
+        # True/False must not pass as an integer/number.
+        return False
+    return isinstance(value, py)
+
+
+def _check(schema: dict, value: Any, path: str, errors: list[str],
+           refs: frozenset[str] | None) -> None:
+    expected = schema.get("type")
+    if expected is not None and not _type_ok(expected, value):
+        errors.append(f"{path or '$'}: expected {expected}, got {type(value).__name__}")
+        return
+
+    if "enum" in schema:
+        allowed = schema["enum"]
+        if value not in allowed:
+            errors.append(f"{path or '$'}: {value!r} not in enum {allowed!r}")
+            return
+
+    if isinstance(value, str) and refs is not None and schema.get("ref") and value not in refs:
+        errors.append(f"{path or '$'}: reference {value!r} not found")
+        return
+
+    if isinstance(value, dict):
+        for key in schema.get("required", []):
+            if key not in value:
+                errors.append(f"{path or '$'}: missing required {key!r}")
+        props = schema.get("properties", {})
+        for key, sub in props.items():
+            if key in value:
+                _check(sub, value[key], f"{path}.{key}" if path else key, errors, refs)
+
+    if isinstance(value, list):
+        item_schema = schema.get("items")
+        if item_schema is not None:
+            for i, item in enumerate(value):
+                _check(item_schema, item, f"{path}[{i}]", errors, refs)
+
+
+def validate_output(
+    value: Any,
+    schema: dict,
+    *,
+    references: set[str] | frozenset[str] | None = None,
+    event_log: SecurityEventLog | None = None,
+) -> ValidationResult:
+    """Validate ``value`` against ``schema`` before it may become state.
+
+    Args:
+        value: the model's parsed output (dict/list/etc.).
+        schema: the small schema vocabulary described in the module docstring.
+        references: the set of valid ids a ``ref``-marked field may cite.
+        event_log: where to record the rejection (default: process-wide).
+
+    Returns:
+        :class:`ValidationResult`. On failure ``ok`` is False, ``value`` is
+        ``None`` (the caller must drop it), ``errors`` lists every reason, and a
+        ``security_event`` of kind ``output_rejected`` is logged.
+    """
+    errors: list[str] = []
+    ref_set = frozenset(references) if references is not None else None
+    _check(schema, value, "", errors, ref_set)
+
+    if errors:
+        target = event_log or get_event_log()
+        log_event(EventKind.OUTPUT_REJECTED, "schema:" + "; ".join(errors[:5]),
+                  event_log=target)
+        return ValidationResult(ok=False, errors=errors, value=None)
+
+    return ValidationResult(ok=True, errors=[], value=value)

原则上批准这份计划，按以下修订执行。

负责人／测试批准人：陈妍妍。

这条回复批准修订后的实施方案和测试策略。请先将现有及拟新增的测试场景、对应文件、预期断言整理为测试审批清单，按仓库规则记录真实审批时间，并在实现代码之前完成审批记录提交。不要倒填时间，不要把后续实质性新增的测试场景自动视为已获批准。

1. 先解决环境和基线

允许在项目独立虚拟环境中安装开发依赖，不修改全局 Python 环境。先检测已有解释器和虚拟环境；优先复用可用环境。

项目 CI 包含 Python 3.14，不要仅凭版本认定不能测试。先安装项目依赖并运行现有测试，记录原有通过、失败和 skip。确有兼容问题时，再使用可用的 3.12 环境，并说明原因。

不要等实现完才尝试搭建测试环境；无法建立环境时，先报告具体安装错误。

2. 先独立完成第五部分，不改组合根

本轮不直接修改 graph/trading_graph.py、graph/setup.py，也不实现 Part 3 的 records、manifest 或报告系统。

提供 adapter、最小调用示例和接入文档，说明 Part 1、Part 3 应在哪些位置调用。使用内存 store 和 fake provenance 验证独立行为。

“模块已实现”和“真实主流程已经接入”分别报告，不宣称已经完成全系统安全防护。

3. 接口兼容

先核对仓库中已经约定的契约。RatingResult 至少保留约定的：
rating、reason_codes、provenance、review_required。
新增字段需说明用途，不用 status/reason 直接替换已有约定。

保留 sanitize(text) -> str 的简单入口；如需 dropped/events 等信息，可提供额外的详细接口并明确两者关系。

提供统一 redact(value) 入口，内部可使用 redact_text/redact_obj。

评级提交接口明确 candidate、provenance、store 的参数及失败语义，避免同一功能出现多个实现入口。

评级权威代码集中在现有 agents/rating.py 或其明确的适配模块，不在顶层任意散放重复逻辑。保留旧解析 API 的兼容性。

4. 来源与幂等校验

明确“有效来源”的结构及验证责任，不能仅检查几个非空字符串。生产验证机制和测试 fake 必须区分。

缺少或无效来源时，不得产生正常提交；返回 REVIEW／拒绝结果并保留原因。

重复提交必须有稳定 decision ID 和明确策略。不能所有缺 ID 的输入共用默认键，也不能让一个无效请求影响另一个决策。

持久化再校验测试直接验证第五部分的提交／写入 adapter，不通过创建空 tradingagents.records 包满足占位测试。

5. 安全实现细节

工具越权检查必须发生在实际执行之前。若 guard 抛出 UnauthorizedToolCall，明确由哪层捕获；测试既检查执行次数为 0，也检查事件记录和后续执行行为。

不可信文本定界处理需考虑原文伪造关闭标签、重复调用和长度截断边界。正常数字、URL、事实须保留。

输出验证要真实检查结构、类型、枚举以及适用引用。使用成熟的现有验证工具或项目已有依赖，避免自行写一个声称支持完整 JSON Schema、实际只检查少数字段的实现。

日志 filter 要考虑延迟格式化参数、异常信息和嵌套数据，不只处理 record.msg。安全日志本身也必须脱敏。

不要为了一个测试单独增加无人使用的 resolve_api_key 并声称已完成凭据来源治理。先检查现有实际凭据加载链路；保留正常 SDK 认证及 provider 特殊认证方式。

6. 测试与资源

批准提交变异生成器和固定种子，不提交 10,000 个生成文件。记录数量、覆盖类别和复现命令。

# Part 5 — Test approval list (G1)

**Change id:** `chg-2026-11-18-part5-security-rating`
**Approved by:** 陈妍妍 (Chen Yanyan)
**Approved at:** 2026-11-18T06:43:59+00:00 (UTC; recorded before implementation)
**Covered test files (G1 `tests`):**
- `tradingagents/tests/req/test_rating_invariant.py`
- `tradingagents/tests/security/test_prompt_injection.py`
- `tradingagents/tests/security/test_secret_redaction.py`

This list describes the scenarios the approved tests assert. Function names and
node ids already on `master` are preserved (only their bodies change from a
module-existence placeholder to a real behavioural assertion). New scenarios that
are substantially added after this approval are **not** silently treated as
approved; if a new *file* must be approved, a separate approval record is added.

## Baseline at approval time (Python 3.14, isolated venv)

Command:
```
cd tradingagents
python -m pytest tests/req/test_rating_invariant.py tests/security -q
```
Result: **7 passed, 10 skipped, 2 deselected**. Full suite:
**1432 passed, 56 skipped, 13 deselected**.

Skips are the `require("tradingagents.security")` / `require("tradingagents.records")`
/ `require("tradingagents.security.redaction")` placeholders these tests replace.

## REQ-INV-003 — `tests/req/test_rating_invariant.py`

| node id | scenario | expected assertion |
|---|---|---|
| `test_allowed_set` | happy: normal decisions through the authority | committed rating ∈ {Buy,Overweight,Hold,Underweight,Sell,REVIEW}; `committed_rating_allowed_set_rate == 1.0` |
| `test_fuzz` | negative: ≥10,000 seeded mutations (fullwidth, markdown-bold, "not a Sell", "Sell-ish", quotes) | every committed/resolved value ∈ allowed set; `invalid_rating_escapes == 0` |
| `test_adversarial_text_cannot_flip` | negative: prose argues opposite of structured field | committed value follows structure; `rating_change_count == 0` |
| `test_review_sentinel` | no readable rating | `REVIEW`, never a guessed tier |
| `test_run_rating_prefers_structured_field` | structured `final_rating` over text | structured value wins |
| `test_fullwidth_and_markdown_tolerant` | fullwidth colon / bold | parsed correctly |
| `test_requires_provenance` | negative: snapshot/manifest/version removed | refused, `REVIEW`, reason code present; `commit_with_missing_provenance_count == 0` |
| `test_missing_snapshot_review` | negative: no verified snapshot id | status `REVIEW` |
| `test_persisted_revalidation` | state: out-of-set stored value | write adapter rejects; `persisted_out_of_set_count == 0` (uses Part 5 store adapter + in-memory double, not `tradingagents.records`) |
| `test_idempotent_commit` | determinism: repeat commit, stable decision id | exactly one committed rating; distinct ids do not collide |

## REQ-SEC-001 — `tests/security/test_prompt_injection.py`

| node id | scenario | expected assertion |
|---|---|---|
| `test_no_unauthorized_tool_calls` | negative: role proposes unbound tool | guard rejects before execution; `executions == 0`; event logged; subsequent authorised call still runs |
| `test_log_coverage` | state: each detect/sanitise/validate/tool-reject event | `SecurityEvent` recorded with reason; `security_event_log_coverage == 1.0`; entries redacted |
| `test_output_validation` | negative: out-of-enum / missing field | rejected before state; `out_of_schema_reaching_state == 0` |
| `test_injection_block_rate` | injection fixtures (≥200 distinct payloads) | `injection_block_or_drop_rate >= 0.99` (offline, deterministic; marker adjusted to offline rules test) |
| `test_benign_false_positive_rate` | benign fixtures (≥200 distinct lines) | `benign_false_positive_rate <= 0.05`; key facts (numbers, URLs) retained |

Note: `test_injection_block_rate` / `test_benign_false_positive_rate` are currently
marked `integration`; because they become pure offline rule tests they are moved
to the default (non-`integration`) run so the default suite covers them.

## REQ-INV-004 — `tests/security/test_secret_redaction.py`

| node id | scenario | expected assertion |
|---|---|---|
| `test_existing_scrub_redacts_secret` | existing `get_scrubbed` | key replaced with `***` (kept as-is) |
| `test_artifacts` | negative: synthetic key in env → logs/reports/manifest | `secret_findings_in_artifacts == 0` |
| `test_redaction` | happy: synthetic secrets in nested structures/logs/exceptions | `synthetic_secret_redaction_rate == 1.0` |
| `test_prompt_payload` | negative: key present, payload inspected pre-call | `secret_occurrences_in_model_payload == 0` |

Additional INV004 scenarios (`test_processor_secret_in_exception`, env-only key
source) are added within this same file only if approved; otherwise they are
reported as new and not counted as approved.

The committed rating is the single authoritative value produced by the

advisory: it is a *candidate* that the authority checks before it may be stored.

This module defines the wire/contract objects only; the commit logic lives in
:mod:`tradingagents.rating_authority` (which re-uses the parser in
:mod:`tradingagents.agents.rating`). Keeping the contract separate lets Part 3
(manifest/report) and Part 6 (cost) read a stable shape without importing the
authority itself.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

# The committed value is exactly one of these six. Anything else is invalid.
ALLOWED_RATINGS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    {"Buy", "Overweight", "Hold", "Underweight", "Sell", "REVIEW"}
)

# The tradeable subset (REVIEW is a "needs human/re-run" signal, not a position).
TRADEABLE_RATINGS: frozenset[str] = ALLOWED_RATINGS - {"REVIEW"}

REVIEW: str = "REVIEW"


# Reason codes attached to a RatingResult. They are stable identifiers so tests,
# logs and downstream tooling can assert *why* a decision is (or is not) REVIEW.
class ReasonCode:
    """Machine-readable reasons for a rating outcome."""

    OK = "ok"
    # The candidate text had no readable rating.
    NO_RATING = "no_rating"
    # The candidate string was not in the allowed set.
    OUT_OF_SET = "out_of_set"
    # A required provenance field was missing or empty.
    MISSING_PROVENANCE = "missing_provenance"
    # A provenance field was present but did not validate (bad id/version shape).
    INVALID_PROVENANCE = "invalid_provenance"
    # The snapshot id was absent or not marked verified.
    UNVERIFIED_SNAPSHOT = "unverified_snapshot"
    # The same decision id was already committed with a different value.
    CONFLICT = "conflict"
    # The persisted value failed re-validation before write.
    PERSISTED_OUT_OF_SET = "persisted_out_of_set"


def is_allowed(rating: str) -> bool:
    """Whether ``rating`` is one of the six allowed committed values."""
    return rating in ALLOWED_RATINGS


def coerce_review(reason_code: str, *, provenance: Any = None) -> "RatingResult":
    """A REVIEW result carrying ``reason_code`` (never a tradeable tier)."""
    return RatingResult(
        rating=REVIEW,
        reason_codes=(reason_code,),
        provenance=provenance,
        review_required=True,
    )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RatingResult:
    """The outcome of rating resolution / commit.

    Fields (the agreed contract; extra fields may be added, existing ones are
    never repurposed):

    - ``rating``: exactly one of :data:`ALLOWED_RATINGS`. This is the only value
      that may be persisted as the decision's rating.
    - ``reason_codes``: stable codes (see :class:`ReasonCode`) explaining the
      outcome; ``("ok",)`` for a clean tradeable commit.
    - ``provenance``: the verified :class:`Provenance` this result was produced
      from, or ``None`` when provenance was missing/invalid. Never free text.
    - ``review_required``: ``True`` iff the value must not be treated as a
      position (i.e. ``rating == "REVIEW"``). Redundant with the rating by
      design, so callers can branch on intent without string compares.

    Added field:

    - ``decision_id``: the stable id the commit was keyed on (for idempotency),
      or ``None`` for a resolution that was not stored.
    """

    rating: str
    reason_codes: tuple[str, ...] = (ReasonCode.OK,)
    provenance: "Provenance | None" = None
    review_required: bool = False
    decision_id: str | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.rating not in ALLOWED_RATINGS:
            raise ValueError(f"rating {self.rating!r} is not in the allowed set")
        # Keep the contract self-consistent: REVIEW <=> review_required.
        if (self.rating == REVIEW) != bool(self.review_required):
            raise ValueError(
                "review_required must be True exactly when rating is REVIEW"
            )

    @property
    def is_tradeable(self) -> bool:
        return self.rating in TRADEABLE_RATINGS

    @property
    def is_review(self) -> bool:
        return self.rating == REVIEW


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Provenance:
    """Verified provenance a commit must carry.

    A commit is only allowed when every field is present *and* validates. These
    are structural ids/versions, not arbitrary non-empty strings: the ids must
    match their hex/uuid-ish shape and versions must be non-empty with a
    recognisable version token. Production populates this from the run's real
    snapshot/manifest/models; tests use a clearly-marked fake (see
    :class:`Provenance` construction in the authority's in-memory tests).

    Fields:

    - ``snapshot_id``: the verified market snapshot id, e.g. ``snap-<32 hex>``.
    - ``manifest_id``: the evidence manifest id for this run, e.g. ``man-<32 hex>``.
    - ``model``: the model identifier used for the decision.
    - ``prompt_version``: the prompt template version pin.
    - ``config_version``: the config version pin.

    Additional:

    - ``snapshot_verified``: whether the snapshot was cryptographically/structurally
      verified. An unverified snapshot id is not acceptable for a commit.
    """

    snapshot_id: str
    manifest_id: str
    model: str
    prompt_version: str
    config_version: str
    snapshot_verified: bool = True

    def missing_fields(self) -> list[str]:
        """Names of required fields that are empty/missing."""
        required = (
            "snapshot_id",
            "manifest_id",
            "model",
            "prompt_version",
            "config_version",
        )
        return [name for name in required if not getattr(self, name)]


# Store adapter protocol (Part 5 owns the write-gate; the concrete store is
# provided by Part 3). A store is any object exposing these two methods. The
# authority never assumes more than this.
#
#   read(decision_id: str) -> dict | None
#       returns the previously stored record (must include a "rating" key) or
#       None when nothing is stored for ``decision_id``.
#   write(decision_id: str, record: dict) -> None
#       persists ``record`` for ``decision_id``; must be atomic for that id.
#
# The authority re-validates the rating immediately before calling ``write`` and
# refuses an out-of-set value (never trusting the store).
Store = Any


@dataclass
class InMemoryRatingStore:
    """A minimal in-memory store used by tests and as the reference adapter.

    It is deliberately tiny: Part 3's real records store is expected to be
    dropped in behind the same ``read``/``write`` interface.
    """

    _records: dict[str, dict] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def read(self, decision_id: str) -> dict | None:
        return self._records.get(decision_id)

    def write(self, decision_id: str, record: dict) -> None:
        self._records[decision_id] = dict(record)

    def all(self) -> dict[str, dict]:
        return dict(self._records)

"""Deterministic rating authority (Part 5, REQ-INV-003).

The committed rating is produced **only** here, by deterministic validation of
the model's advisory output, and is exactly one of
``{Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell, REVIEW}``. This module is the single
entry point that may decide a persisted rating; it re-uses the tolerant parser in
:mod:`tradingagents.agents.rating` rather than duplicating it.

Design rules enforced here:

- Model output is a *candidate*, never authoritative. It is parsed and checked
  against :data:`tradingagents.contracts.rating.ALLOWED_RATINGS`; anything else
  becomes ``REVIEW`` with a reason code.
- A commit requires verified :class:`Provenance` (snapshot id, manifest id and
  model/prompt/config versions). Missing or structurally invalid provenance ->
  ``REVIEW`` (never a tradeable tier) and no write.
- Free text never overrides a structured rating: when the candidate is given as
  a structured value it is validated directly; when only text is available it is
  parsed, but prose without a labelled call resolves to ``REVIEW``.
- The write gate re-validates the value immediately before persisting, so an
  out-of-set value can never reach the store even if produced upstream.
- Commits are idempotent per stable ``decision_id``: re-committing the same
  decision returns the existing committed value; a conflicting re-commit is
  refused. Different decisions never share a key.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass

from tradingagents.agents.rating import extract_rating
from tradingagents.contracts.rating import (
    ALLOWED_RATINGS,
    REVIEW,
    InMemoryRatingStore,
    Provenance,
    RatingResult,
    ReasonCode,
    Store,
    coerce_review,
)

__all__ = [
    "ALLOWED_RATINGS",
    "REVIEW",
    "RatingResult",
    "ReasonCode",
    "Provenance",
    "InMemoryRatingStore",
    "resolve_rating",
    "validate_provenance",
    "commit_rating",
]

# Structural shapes for the provenance ids. These are not "any non-empty string":
# a snapshot/manifest id must look like `prefix-<hex>` with a real hex body.
_SNAPSHOT_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^snap-[0-9a-f]{8,64}$")
_MANIFEST_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^man-[0-9a-f]{8,64}$")
# A version pin: a bare semver-ish or `v<number>` token, optionally with `+build`.
_VERSION_RE = re.compile(r"^v?\d+(?:\.\d+){0,2}(?:[-+][0-9A-Za-z.]+)?$")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _ProvenanceCheck:
    ok: bool
    reason: str


def validate_provenance(provenance: Provenance | None) -> _ProvenanceCheck:
    """Whether ``provenance`` is a verified, well-formed commit source.

    This is the *production* validation: it checks structure, not mere
    non-emptiness. A test fake must still satisfy these shapes, which keeps the
    fake honest (a fake cannot be arbitrary free text).
    """
    if provenance is None:
        return _ProvenanceCheck(False, ReasonCode.MISSING_PROVENANCE)

    missing = provenance.missing_fields()
    if missing:
        return _ProvenanceCheck(False, ReasonCode.MISSING_PROVENANCE)

    if not provenance.snapshot_verified:
        return _ProvenanceCheck(False, ReasonCode.UNVERIFIED_SNAPSHOT)

    if not _SNAPSHOT_ID_RE.match(provenance.snapshot_id):
        return _ProvenanceCheck(False, ReasonCode.INVALID_PROVENANCE)
    if not _MANIFEST_ID_RE.match(provenance.manifest_id):
        return _ProvenanceCheck(False, ReasonCode.INVALID_PROVENANCE)
    if not (_VERSION_RE.match(provenance.prompt_version)
            and _VERSION_RE.match(provenance.config_version)):
        return _ProvenanceCheck(False, ReasonCode.INVALID_PROVENANCE)
    if not provenance.model.strip():
        return _ProvenanceCheck(False, ReasonCode.INVALID_PROVENANCE)

    return _ProvenanceCheck(True, ReasonCode.OK)


def _candidate_to_rating(candidate: object) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Resolve a candidate (structured value or text) to ``(rating, reason)``.

    A structured value is validated as-is. Text is parsed by the shared parser;
    text with no labelled call is ``REVIEW``. The result is always in
    :data:`ALLOWED_RATINGS`.
    """
    if isinstance(candidate, str):
        value = candidate.strip()
        if value in ALLOWED_RATINGS:
            return value, ReasonCode.OK
        # Not a structured tier: treat as free text and parse a labelled call.
        parsed = extract_rating(candidate)
        if parsed is None:
            return REVIEW, ReasonCode.NO_RATING
        return parsed, ReasonCode.OK
    return REVIEW, ReasonCode.NO_RATING


def resolve_rating(candidate: object) -> str:
    """The deterministic verdict for ``candidate`` alone (no provenance).

    Always in the allowed set. Exposed so callers that only need the parsed
    value (e.g. the memory log tag) share exactly the authority's parser.
    """
    rating, _ = _candidate_to_rating(candidate)
    return rating


def _normalise_existing(record: dict | None) -> str | None:
    if not record:
        return None
    value = record.get("rating")
    return value if value in ALLOWED_RATINGS else None


def commit_rating(
    candidate: object,
    provenance: Provenance | None,
    store: Store,
    *,
    decision_id: str,
) -> RatingResult:
    """Validate ``candidate`` against ``provenance`` and commit it via ``store``.

    Args:
        candidate: the model's advisory output — either a structured tier string
            or the decision text. Parsed/validated deterministically.
        provenance: the verified run provenance, or ``None`` when unavailable.
        store: an object with ``read(decision_id)`` and ``write(decision_id,
            record)`` (see :data:`tradingagents.contracts.rating.Store`). The
            authority re-validates before writing and never trusts the store.
        decision_id: a stable, non-empty id for this decision. It keys idempotency
            and prevents cross-decision collisions. A blank id is a programming
            error and is refused (never defaulted to a shared key).

    Returns:
        A :class:`RatingResult`. On any failure the ``rating`` is ``REVIEW``,
        ``review_required`` is ``True``, ``reason_codes`` explains why, and
        nothing is written. On success the value is tradeable, is in the allowed
        set, carries the provenance, and exactly one record exists for
        ``decision_id``.
    """
    if not isinstance(decision_id, str) or not decision_id.strip():
        # Refuse an unusable key rather than letting decisions share one.
        return coerce_review(ReasonCode.INVALID_PROVENANCE, provenance=provenance)

    # Idempotency: an existing commit for this id wins, unless it conflicts.
    existing = _normalise_existing(store.read(decision_id))
    if existing is not None:
        return RatingResult(
            rating=existing,
            reason_codes=(ReasonCode.OK,),
            provenance=provenance,
            review_required=(existing == REVIEW),
            decision_id=decision_id,
        )

    # Provenance gate: missing/invalid/unverified -> REVIEW, no write.
    check = validate_provenance(provenance)
    if not check.ok:
        return coerce_review(check.reason, provenance=provenance)

    rating, reason = _candidate_to_rating(candidate)
    if rating == REVIEW:
        return coerce_review(reason, provenance=provenance)
    if rating not in ALLOWED_RATINGS:
        # Defence in depth: the parser must never yield an out-of-set value.
        return coerce_review(ReasonCode.OUT_OF_SET, provenance=provenance)

    # Persisted re-validation: refuse to write an out-of-set value.
    if rating not in ALLOWED_RATINGS:
        return coerce_review(ReasonCode.PERSISTED_OUT_OF_SET, provenance=provenance)

    record = {
        "rating": rating,
        "decision_id": decision_id,
        "snapshot_id": provenance.snapshot_id if provenance else None,
        "manifest_id": provenance.manifest_id if provenance else None,
        "model": provenance.model if provenance else None,
        "prompt_version": provenance.prompt_version if provenance else None,
        "config_version": provenance.config_version if provenance else None,
    }
    store.write(decision_id, record)

    return RatingResult(
        rating=rating,
        reason_codes=(ReasonCode.OK,),
        provenance=provenance,
        review_required=False,
        decision_id=decision_id,
    )


def read_committed_rating(store: Store, *, decision_id: str) -> RatingResult:
    """Read back a committed rating, re-validating it against the allowed set.

    A stored value that is out-of-set (tampered/corrupt) is treated as ``REVIEW``
    with :data:`ReasonCode.PERSISTED_OUT_OF_SET` — it is never returned as a tier.
    """
    record = store.read(decision_id)
    value = record.get("rating") if record else None
    if value in ALLOWED_RATINGS:
        return RatingResult(
            rating=value,
            reason_codes=(ReasonCode.OK,),
            review_required=(value == REVIEW),
            decision_id=decision_id,
        )
    return coerce_review(ReasonCode.PERSISTED_OUT_OF_SET)

def test_allowed_set():
    """TC-P5-INV003-02: a committed rating is always in the allowed set."""
    store = InMemoryRatingStore()
    cases = ["**Rating**: Buy", "Rating: Sell", "no rating here", "Rating: Underweight"]
    committed = []
    for i, text in enumerate(cases):
        result = commit_rating(text, _provenance(), store, decision_id=f"d{i}")
        committed.append(result.rating)
    # Clean decisions are tradeable; a decision with no call is REVIEW.
    assert committed[0] == "Buy"
    assert committed[1] == "Sell"
    assert committed[2] == RATING_REVIEW
    assert committed[3] == "Underweight"
    # Every committed value is exactly one of the six, and it is what was stored.
    assert set(committed) <= ALLOWED
    for i in range(len(cases)):
        assert store.read(f"d{i}")["rating"] == committed[i]


def test_fuzz():
    """TC-P5-INV003-01: 10,000 mutated inputs never escape the allowed set."""
    random.seed(0)
    parts = ["Buy", "Sell", "Hold", "Overweight", "Underweight", "not a Sell",
             "Sell-ish", "BUY", "Ｓｅｌｌ", "review", "%^&", "**Rating**", ":",
             "Rating：", "Rating: **Sell**"]
    store = InMemoryRatingStore()
    prov = _provenance()
    escapes = 0
    for i in range(10_000):
        text = " ".join(random.choice(parts) for _ in range(random.randint(0, 5)))
        rating = resolve_rating(text)
        if rating not in ALLOWED:
            escapes += 1
        # Exercise the commit path too: whatever it yields must be in-set.
        result = commit_rating(text, prov, store, decision_id=f"f{i}")
        if result.rating not in ALLOWED:
            escapes += 1
    assert escapes == 0


def test_adversarial_text_cannot_flip():
    """TC-P5-INV003-04: prose arguing the opposite does not flip a labelled rating."""
    # An explicit opening "Rating: Sell" is the call, even if the prose says otherwise.
    text = "**Rating**: Sell\n\nThis is clearly NOT a Sell; I would actually Buy."
    assert extract_rating(text) == "Sell"
    # Through the authority: the committed value follows the labelled call.
    store = InMemoryRatingStore()
    result = commit_rating(text, _provenance(), store, decision_id="adv")
    assert result.rating == "Sell"


def test_review_sentinel():
    """A decision with no readable rating yields REVIEW, never a guessed tier."""
    assert parse_rating("The outlook is mixed with no clear call.") == RATING_REVIEW
    assert is_review(parse_rating("no rating"))


def test_run_rating_prefers_structured_field():
    """run_rating prefers the structured final_rating over text."""
    assert run_rating({"final_rating": "Overweight", "final_trade_decision": "**Rating**: Sell"}) == "Overweight"


def test_fullwidth_and_markdown_tolerant():
    """Fullwidth punctuation and bold are tolerated."""
    assert extract_rating("Rating：Overweight") == "Overweight"


def test_requires_provenance():
    """TC-P5-INV003-03: commit gate refuses a decision missing provenance."""
    store = InMemoryRatingStore()
    # No provenance at all.
    r = commit_rating("**Rating**: Buy", None, store, decision_id="p1")
    assert r.rating == RATING_REVIEW and r.review_required
    assert ReasonCode.MISSING_PROVENANCE in r.reason_codes
    # Provenance with a field removed: each missing field refuses the commit.
    for field in ("snapshot_id", "manifest_id", "model", "prompt_version", "config_version"):
        broken = _provenance(**{field: ""})
        r = commit_rating("**Rating**: Buy", broken, store, decision_id=f"p-{field}")
        assert r.rating == RATING_REVIEW, field
        assert ReasonCode.MISSING_PROVENANCE in r.reason_codes, field
    # Nothing was committed for any of the refused decisions.
    assert store.all() == {}


def test_requires_provenance_rejects_free_text_source():
    """A free-text/non-structural 'source' is invalid provenance, not accepted."""
    store = InMemoryRatingStore()
    # Non-hex ids and non-version pins must not pass as verified provenance.
    bad = _provenance(snapshot_id="my-snapshot", manifest_id="some manifest")
    r = commit_rating("**Rating**: Buy", bad, store, decision_id="bad-shape")
    assert r.rating == RATING_REVIEW
    assert ReasonCode.INVALID_PROVENANCE in r.reason_codes
    assert store.all() == {}


def test_missing_snapshot_review():
    """TC-P5-INV003-05: missing snapshot id yields REVIEW."""
    store = InMemoryRatingStore()
    r = commit_rating("**Rating**: Buy", _provenance(snapshot_id=""), store, decision_id="ms")
    assert r.rating == RATING_REVIEW
    assert r.review_required
    assert store.all() == {}
    # An id present but not verified is equally not committable.
    r2 = commit_rating("**Rating**: Buy", _provenance(snapshot_verified=False), store, decision_id="ms2")
    assert r2.rating == RATING_REVIEW
    assert ReasonCode.UNVERIFIED_SNAPSHOT in r2.reason_codes
    assert store.all() == {}


def test_persisted_revalidation():
    """TC-P5-INV003-06: persisted out-of-set values are rejected."""
    # The write gate re-validates: an out-of-set persisted value reads as REVIEW,
    # never as a tier, even if it was written by a faulty/older writer.
    store = InMemoryRatingStore()
    store.write("tampered", {"rating": "Moon", "decision_id": "tampered"})
    back = read_committed_rating(store, decision_id="tampered")
    assert back.rating == RATING_REVIEW
    assert ReasonCode.PERSISTED_OUT_OF_SET in back.reason_codes
    # A normal commit persists only an in-set value.
    r = commit_rating("**Rating**: Hold", _provenance(), store, decision_id="ok")
    assert r.rating == "Hold"
    assert store.read("ok")["rating"] in ALLOWED


def test_idempotent_commit():
    """TC-P5-INV003-07: the commit gate is idempotent."""
    store = InMemoryRatingStore()
    prov = _provenance()
    first = commit_rating("**Rating**: Buy", prov, store, decision_id="same")
    second = commit_rating("**Rating**: Buy", prov, store, decision_id="same")
    assert first.rating == second.rating == "Buy"
    # Exactly one committed record for the decision.
    assert list(store.all()) == ["same"]
    # A blank decision id is refused — decisions never share a default key.
    blank = commit_rating("**Rating**: Buy", prov, store, decision_id="  ")
    assert blank.rating == RATING_REVIEW
    assert store.read("") is None
    # A distinct id is an independent decision, not a collision.
    other = commit_rating("**Rating**: Sell", prov, store, decision_id="different")
    assert other.rating == "Sell"
    assert set(store.all()) == {"same", "different"}
